title: A fake clock
hints: The closure `func() time.Time { return now }` reads the variable `now` every time it is called. Assigning a new value to `now` in your test "moves the clock" for the session too.

Bugs hide at the deadline: check `Expired` and `Remaining` at `start + ttl - 1ns`, at exactly `start + ttl`, and later. For `Touch`, call it partway through, then check just before and exactly at `touch time + ttl`.

```go
start := time.Date(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
now := start
s := New(time.Hour, func() time.Time { return now })

now = start.Add(time.Hour - time.Nanosecond)
if s.Expired() { t.Errorf("Expired() 1ns before the deadline = true, want false") }
now = start.Add(time.Hour)
if !s.Expired() { t.Errorf("Expired() at the deadline = false, want true") }
if got := s.Remaining(); got != 0 { t.Errorf("Remaining() = %v, want 0s", got) }
```
Then do the same around a `Touch()` at `start + 40m` (new deadline `start + 1h40m`).
